explore.curve_partial_meaning: Some targets have a verified build, but others are unresolved or failed (see coverage details). The curve may be missing points.
explore.curve_infeasible_meaning: Every scheduled target was proved to have no build.
explore.curve_invalid_meaning: No target produced a verified build, and some were unresolved, failed or never ran (or the request was rejected).

optimize.ready_description: Selecciona arma y ajusta prioridades para generar build óptima
optimize.true_ergo_tooltip: When enabled, the ergonomics weight optimizes TrueErgo Delta (TED), not raw ergonomics. E = clamp(clamp(raw ergo, 0, 100) × (1+b), 0, 100); TED = E − max(0, 100 − 300/W), with W in kg. At W ≤ 3, TED = E. Gear modifiers apply to the TED objective and overswing constraint. Works with augmented Tchebycheff.
optimize.tchebycheff_tooltip: Optimiza las configuraciones más eficientes equilibrando ergonomía, retroceso y precio simultáneamente, encontrando soluciones intermedias de gran valor.

constraints.exact_moa_floor_tooltip: When on, the slider's minimum comes from the solver: the smallest MOA your other constraints allow under the provisional MOA model (slower, up to 30 s). When off, the minimum is a theoretical estimate that may not be reachable.
constraints.prevent_overswing_tooltip: Requires W × (1 − E/100) ≤ 3, equivalently TED ≥ 0. Equality is not overswing. W is weight in kg; E is gear-adjusted ergonomics clamped to 0–100. This does not impose a 7 kg weight limit.
constraints.equip_ergo_penalty_tooltip: Combined equipment ergonomics modifier: −20% means b = −0.20. Clamp raw ergonomics to 0–100, multiply by (1+b), then clamp again to 0–100. Applies to the TrueErgo objective even when Prevent Overswing is off.

results.authority_incomplete_detail: No verified build was found. This is not a proof that none exists.
results.authority_certified_infeasible_detail: A Precise search proved that no build satisfies all of these constraints. Loosen one and try again.

results.qualifier_provisional_moa_tooltip: This result depends on a MOA limit. MOA comes from a provisional model, so a result that uses it is never presented as proved.
results.one_copy_per_part_tooltip: This Fast result uses at most one of each part. Turn on Allow repeated parts under Advanced to allow repeats.

methodology.title: Guide & Methodology
methodology.ergo_desc: In Escape from Tarkov, raw Ergonomics directly controls the ADS (Aim Down Sights) animation duration and the audio cue loudness when scoping in.
methodology.true_ergo_desc_1: TrueErgo uses weapon weight W in kg and effective ergonomics E. The model predicts overswing only when this strict inequality holds; equality is safe:
methodology.true_ergo_desc_2: TrueErgo Delta is the difference between effective ergonomics and the minimum ergonomics needed to prevent overswing. Its unit is ergonomics points, not kilograms:
methodology.ted_positive: TED ≥ 0: The model predicts no overswing, including the boundary.
methodology.true_ergo_light_label: Light weapons need no overswing threshold deduction:
methodology.equip_penalty_desc_1: The equipment ergonomics modifier b applies after raw ergonomics is clamped to 0–100. The result is clamped again to 0–100:
methodology.equip_penalty_desc_2: This effective ergonomics is used for both TED optimization and overswing validation. TrueErgo applies the equipment modifier even when Prevent Overswing is disabled.
methodology.moa_desc: Tarkov stores spread as centerOfImpact (COI); the app converts it to in-game MOA (Minute of Angle) with K = 100 / 2.9089 ≈ 34.377. This is a provisional model (see below):
methodology.moa_barrel_note: For weapons with replaceable barrels (e.g. M700, VPO-215), installing a barrel replaces the intrinsic weapon COI.
methodology.mip_desc: Slot dependencies, parent-child placements, conflicts and preset bundles are compiled into a mixed-integer linear program and solved with HiGHS (WebAssembly) in a browser Web Worker, with no backend. Precise mode gives every installed copy of a part its own physical slot, so repeated parts are separate occurrences.
methodology.sweet_spot_alert_title: Why standard weighted sums miss 45%–61% of optimal builds
methodology.sweet_spot_alert_desc: In standard weighted sum optimization, the objective is a flat rotating hyperplane. Because weapon mod trees feature discrete prerequisites and step-function pricing, the Pareto frontier is non-convex. Flat hyperplanes can only touch the outer convex hull, jumping abruptly between budget and meta builds while skipping high-efficiency intermediate configurations.
methodology.sweet_spot_how: Augmented Tchebycheff minimizes the largest weighted normalized gap from the ideal point, plus a small weighted sum of gaps. With TrueErgo enabled, the ergonomics axis uses gear-adjusted TED alongside recoil and price:
methodology.sweet_spot_contour: Corner-shaped contours can find nonconvex tradeoffs skipped by linear weights. A finite search does not enumerate the whole Pareto frontier; optimality depends on the reported bounds, gap, and termination status.
methodology.explore_desc: Explore solves one objective at its two extremes, then steps a limit on the swept axis between them, with one full solve per target. Each target ends as a verified build, a proof that none exists, unresolved, or failed. The curve is Complete when every scheduled target has a build or a proof, Partial when some are unresolved or failed, Infeasible when all are proved empty, and No result otherwise. Complete means the scheduled targets are covered, not that the curve is the continuous Pareto frontier. Points appear live as targets finish, and Cancel keeps the points found so far.
methodology.nonlinear_bounds_desc: TED and overswing feasibility are nonconvex. The solver uses bounded intervals with valid upper and lower bounds, not tangent restrictions as proof of infeasibility or optimality. At a search limit, a verified build is feasible but not proven optimal; without a verified build the result is incomplete, not infeasible. Results show objective bounds, absolute gap, and tolerance.
methodology.data_source_desc: All weapon and mod data is fetched from the Tarkov.dev open JSON API (171 weapons, 2,295 attachments, and barter tables).
methodology.flea_desc: Uses 24-hour average and last low price.
methodology.trader_desc: Strict gating for Prapor, Skier, Peacekeeper, Mechanic, Jaeger, and Ref (LL1–4 or Off).
methodology.barter_desc: Calculated as the total flea market value of required trade-in items.
methodology.presets_desc: The optimizer evaluates both stripped naked receivers and trader weapon presets. A preset supplies its parts at no extra cost, in the quantities it lists; each installed copy is shown as its own part, with how it was supplied (preset, owned or bought). The shopping list adds up to the true spend.
methodology.cache_desc: Game data is cached in IndexedDB for 1 hour. If a game patch drops, click the top-right Force Refresh button to purge local storage, restart the worker, and download fresh data.
methodology.glossary_ted_desc: TED = E − max(0, 100 − 300/W). At W ≤ 3 kg, TED = E. Nonnegative means no overswing in this model; negative means overswing. TED is an ergonomics-point margin, not a fixed per-kilogram exchange rate.
methodology.glossary_moa_desc: Measure of weapon mechanical spread. Lower is more accurate (1 MOA ≈ 1 inch spread at 100 yards).
methodology.glossary_tch_desc: A mathematical scalarization method for non-convex multi-objective optimization that minimizes the worst-case normalized gap from the ideal reference point.
methodology.glossary_forge_desc: Open a build in EFTForge with one click. EFTForge's format cannot name repeated parts or slots, so export is disabled for builds with several copies of one part, with the reason shown. The in-app list is never affected.
methodology.precision_intro: In weapon modding, accessories (such as flashlights, lasers, backup sights, and rail mounts) can fit into multiple candidate slots across different handguards and adapters. This is the multi-slot assignment problem:
methodology.precision_fast: Fast mode: searches a template-count model of the weapon, usually in about a second. The result is approximate and is labelled so (also with TrueErgo and Prevent Overswing, which Fast supports with its own weight search); it is not proved optimal. By default Fast uses at most one of each part; turn on Allow repeated parts under Advanced to allow repeats (Precise always allows them).
methodology.precision_precise: Precise mode: gives every installed copy of a part its own physical slot and returns a proved optimum or a proved infeasibility. TrueErgo and Prevent Overswing run an exact weight search. A large weapon may stop at the time limit, which gives a feasible build or no build, never a false proof.
methodology.precision_auto: Auto mode (default): uses Precise mode for every weapon. With TrueErgo or Prevent Overswing on, the largest weapons (the AK and M4 families) use Fast mode instead, so the answer comes back in time, and are labelled approximate.
methodology.glossary_precision_desc: Auto uses Precise for compact weapons and Fast for very large weapon trees. Precise gives proved results; Fast gives approximate ones.
methodology.moa_provisional_desc: The MOA formula above is a provisional model of the game, not a verified in-game measurement. Any result that depends on a MOA limit is therefore labelled "Provisional MOA model" and is never shown as proved, even when the search itself is exact.
methodology.moa_floor_desc: With the MOA limit on, the app asks the Precise solver for the smallest MOA your other constraints allow, under the provisional model. "Proved" means the minimum is bracketed to within 0.02 MOA. "Best witnessed MOA — minimum not proved" means a build reaching that MOA exists, but a lower one may too (the search ran out of time or stopped early). If no build is found, the slider uses an estimate. The floor is a result of the provisional model, never a game-physical minimum.
methodology.status_title: 6. Result Authority: Proved, Approximate, Feasible, Incomplete
methodology.status_intro: Every result says how much it proves:
methodology.status_certified: Proved optimal / proved infeasible: a Precise search that does not depend on the provisional MOA model finished, and its answer was checked independently.
methodology.status_approximate: Approximate: the search finished, but on an approximate model (Fast) or with a MOA limit (provisional model). A good build, but a better one may exist.
methodology.status_feasible: Feasible: a verified build, but the search stopped (time, node or solution limit, or cancel) before proving it is the best.
methodology.status_incomplete: Incomplete: no verified build was found. This is not a proof that none exists; the reason says what stopped the search.
methodology.glossary_status_desc: How much a result proves. Only a Precise result without a MOA limit can be proved optimal or infeasible; Fast and MOA-dependent results are approximate; a feasible build is verified but unproven; incomplete means no verified build.
methodology.details_hint: Open Details under a result to see the proof status, these bounds and the model notes; the main view keeps to a short, plain summary.

reasons.provisionalMoaModelInfeasible: El modelo MOA provisional no encontró ningún build con ese límite de MOA. Es un resultado del modelo, no una prueba del juego; relaja el límite de MOA u otra restricción.
reasons.fastProvisionalMoaModelInfeasible: El modelo aproximado (rápido) no encontró ningún build con el límite de MOA. Eso no demuestra que no exista; prueba Preciso o relaja el límite de MOA.
reasons.invalidOwnedItems: La lista del alijo no es válida, así que no se resolvió nada.
reasons.invalidExploreSchedule: El plan de exploración está vacío o no es válido, así que no se resolvió nada.
reasons.unsupportedCyclicPartGraph: Los datos de esta arma tienen piezas que pueden montarse unas en otras en bucle; el optimizador no admite esos datos, así que no se resolvió nada.
reasons.queueTimeoutBeforeDispatch: El tiempo de la solicitud se agotó en la cola, así que no se resolvió nada. Inténtalo de nuevo.
reasons.independentBuildValidationFailed: Un build del solucionador no superó la validación independiente, así que se ocultó.
reasons.requiredProofPrerequisiteUnavailable: Faltaba un requisito para una demostración, así que no se afirma ninguna.
reasons.timeLimitReached: Se alcanzó el límite de tiempo.
reasons.nodeLimitReached: Se alcanzó el límite de nodos.
reasons.nativeSolutionLimitReached: Se alcanzó el límite de soluciones del propio solucionador (no es un tiempo de espera).
reasons.advice_timeLimitReached: Vuelve a ejecutar, relaja una restricción o usa el modo Rápido en armas grandes.
reasons.advice_nodeLimitReached: Relaja una restricción o usa el modo Rápido; hacía falta una búsqueda mayor.
reasons.advice_nativeSolutionLimitReached: Es el tope del propio solucionador, no un límite de tiempo. Vuelve a ejecutar para una búsqueda más completa.
